topic: How does an induction stove heat only the pan?

claims.claim: An induction hob has a glass-ceramic surface with a copper coil under each cooking position carrying alternating current.
claims.passage: glass-ceramic surface. Below each cooking position there is a coil of copper wire with an alternating electric current passing through it

claims.claim: The alternating current produces an oscillating magnetic field.
The field induces currents (eddy currents) in the metal bottom of the cookware, which produce heat by flowing through resistance.
claims.passage: induces an electrical current in the metal bottom of the cookware, which produces heat by flowing through resistance ... inducing eddy currents within it

claims.claim: The heat is produced in the cookware's base rather than by a flame or glowing element.
claims.passage: induces an electrical current in the metal bottom of the cookware, which produces heat

guardrails: the glass still warms from contact with the hot pan; narration says heat is produced in the pan, not that the glass stays cold
cookware must contain ferromagnetic metal (not narrated)
field lines and currents are schematic
open_questions: secondary source; native Telugu review of సుడి కరెంట్లు (eddy currents)
